note: Readings where the English has words the recorded Latin lacks and the question is which is right. Needs a printed Clementine Vulgate.

items.latin: At illi dixerunt: In Bethlehem Judæ: sic enim scriptum est per prophetam:
items.english: But they said to him: In Bethlehem of Juda. For so it is written by the prophet:

first_reading.proposed: But they said: In Bethlehem of Juda. For so it is written by the prophet:
first_reading.reason: Latin shown reads "At illi dixerunt:" with no "ei"; the Douay "to him" rests on the reading "dixerunt ei". (If the Clementine source has "ei", the Latin record has dropped it.)

second_reading.note: Card shows 'dixerunt' alone, but the Clementine as I know it reads 'dixerunt ei'; the Latin record probably dropped 'ei', so check it rather than cut 'to him'.

items.status: source check needed: the English has words the recorded Latin lacks; the recorded Latin agrees with the reference transcription, and the second reader recalls a different Clementine reading

items.latin: Respondens autem Petrus, dixit ad Jesum: Domine, bonum est nos hic esse: si vis, faciamus tria tabernacula, tibi unum, Moysi unum, et Eliæ unum.
items.english: And Peter answered to Jesus: Lord, it is good for us to be here: if you will, let us make here three tabernacles, one for you, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah.

first_reading.proposed: And Peter answered to Jesus: Lord, it is good for us to be here: if you will, let us make three tabernacles, one for you, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah.
first_reading.reason: Latin shown reads "si vis, faciamus tria tabernacula" with no second "hic"; "let us make here" follows the Douay/Latin reading "faciamus hic". (If the Clementine source has "hic", the Latin record has dropped it.)

second_reading.note: Card lacks a second 'hic', but the Clementine as I know it reads 'faciamus hic tria tabernacula'; the Latin record probably dropped it, so check it rather than cut 'here'.

items.status: source check needed: the English has words the recorded Latin lacks; the recorded Latin agrees with the reference transcription, and the second reader recalls a different Clementine reading

items.latin: Et quosdam quidem posuit Deus in ecclesia primum apostolos, secundo prophetas, exinde doctores, deinde virtutes, exinde gratias curationum, opitulationes, gubernationes, genera linguarum, interpretationes sermonum.
items.english: And God indeed has set some in the church; first apostles, secondly prophets, thirdly doctors: after that miracles: then the graces of healings, helps, governments, kinds of tongues, interpretations of speeches.

first_reading.proposed: And God indeed has set some in the church; first apostles, secondly prophets, then doctors: after that miracles: then the graces of healings, helps, governments, kinds of tongues, interpretations of speeches.
first_reading.reason: LA shown has 'exinde doctores' (then, after that); EN 'thirdly' renders 'tertio' (Greek triton). If the recorded LA is itself a slip for 'tertio doctores', correct the Latin instead.

second_reading.note: Clementine reads "tertio doctores"; the card's first "exinde" looks like a transcription slip, so "thirdly" is right and the Latin should be fixed instead.

items.status: source check needed: the English has words the recorded Latin lacks; the recorded Latin agrees with the reference transcription, and the second reader recalls a different Clementine reading
